_comment: Azure App Service configuration for the Streamlit container. Apply with `az webapp config set`. NO SECRETS APPEAR HERE - the app authenticates to Blob Storage with its system-assigned managed identity, and any secret it needs is a Key Vault reference resolved at runtime.
name: medsearch-app

appSettings._comment: Matches run_training.py's --mount/data. Holds raw/, interim/, processed/.
appSettings.name: MEDSEARCH_DATA_DIR

artefacts._comment: Read-only blob mount: how the container gets its models and indexes. Databricks writes them here (run_training.py builds Settings with data_dir=$mount/data, model_dir=$mount/models) and the app reads the same layout back. NOTE: App Service storage mounts authenticate with a storage ACCESS KEY, not the managed identity -- Microsoft's docs state that accounts with key-based authentication disabled are unsupported. Put the key in Key Vault and reference it from accessKey; the managed identity still covers everything else the app talks to. Azure Blob mounts are read-only, which is what we want for artefacts.

sku._comment: B2 gives 3.5 GB RAM, comfortably above the 1.2 GB serving budget in Architecture.md section 9. B1 at 1.75 GB is tight once both models are loaded.
sku.name: B2
